decisionTitle: Trailing newline from stdin is stripped before palindrome check; explicit `--out` empty result is still written as a file
rationale: cli.js is a thin I/O layer over the existing palindrome-checker/lib.js (task 16): it parses --text <val>/--text=val, falls back to reading stdin synchronously via fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8') when --text is absent, supports --strict (mapped 1:1 to lib.js's isPalindrome(text, { strict }) option, no signature changes to lib.js), and supports --out <path>/--out=path to redirect the 'yes'/'no' line to a file instead of stdout. Both outcomes set process.exitCode = 0; missing input (neither --text nor non-empty stdin) and PalindromeCheckerError/fs write errors are caught, printed to stderr, and set a non-zero exitCode without throwing an unhandled exception. One deliberate addition beyond the literal spec: stdin input has a single trailing newline (\r?\n+ at the end) stripped before being passed to lib.js, since a typical `echo text | cli.js --strict` invocation would otherwise fail strict mode purely due to the shell-appended newline, which did not seem like the intended behavior of --strict (case/non-letter chars taken literally) versus an artifact of how stdin is piped. --text values are used exactly as given, with no trimming. Added palindrome-checker/test/cli.test.js with node:child_process.spawnSync-based process tests covering --text, --text=, stdin fallback, --strict on/off, --out and --out=, exit code 0 for both yes and no, non-zero exit + stderr message on missing input, and non-zero exit on an unwritable --out path. Full suite (lib.test.js + cli.test.js) via `npm --prefix palindrome-checker test` passes 42/42.
